question: Product Bundle vs. Grouped Product: What's the Difference?
metaDescription: A Grouped Product lists separate products together for individual purchase; a Bundle combines items into one single purchasable product with one price.
shortAnswer: A Grouped Product (a core WooCommerce product type) displays several separate, individually purchasable products together on one page, letting a customer choose quantities of each and add only the ones they want — each item is still bought and priced independently. A Bundle, which needs a dedicated bundling plugin rather than a core product type, combines multiple items into a single product with its own single price and single line item in the cart, typically at a discount compared to buying everything separately.

bodyHtml:
How Each Actually Works

A Grouped Product is one of WooCommerce's core product types, acting as a container that lists other existing simple products together on a single page — a customer sees each item with its own price and a quantity field, and can choose to add any combination of them to the cart, each as its own separate cart line item at its own price. A Bundle, which requires a dedicated bundling plugin since it isn't a built-in product type, packages multiple items into what functions as one single product: one price, one cart line item, and typically a discount reflecting the value of buying the set together rather than piece by piece.

Choosing the Right One

  • Use a Grouped Product when showcasing related items customers might want to mix and match, each purchased and priced individually — a "starter kit" page where someone might only want two of the four listed items.
  • Use a Bundle when the intent is a single fixed-price package sold as one unit — a "starter kit" sold as one product at one discounted price, regardless of whether the customer would have wanted each piece separately.
  • Stock and reporting differ too: a Grouped Product's individual items track their own stock and appear separately in sales reports, while a Bundle's component tracking depends entirely on how the specific bundling plugin implements it.
  • A Bundle generally supports a genuine bundle discount more naturally, since it's priced as a single unit; replicating a true bundle discount with a Grouped Product needs a separate discount mechanism layered on top.

Setting Either Up

  1. For a Grouped Product, create it as a product type directly in core WooCommerce and link the existing simple products you want listed together.
  2. For a Bundle, install a dedicated bundling plugin and configure the specific items, pricing, and any discount for the combined package.
  3. Match the choice to the actual buying intent you want to support — flexible mix-and-match versus one fixed package.
